message.content:
Painting the entire Eiffel Tower would be a massive undertaking. The tower is 324 m (1,063 ft) tall, weighs about 10,100 t, and has roughly 18 000 square metres of exposed metal surface. Even if you had a crew of 50 painters working full‑time, you’d still need several months to finish the job.

A rough breakdown:

| Task | Estimated time (full‑time crew) |
|------|--------------------------------|
| Surface prep (cleaning, rust removal) | 2–3 weeks |
| Primer coat | 1–2 weeks |
| Base coat | 1–2 weeks |
| Topcoat (protective layer) | 1–2 weeks |
| Detail work (corners, railings, decorative elements) | 2–3 weeks |
| Inspection & touch‑ups | 1–2 weeks |

So, from start to finish, you’re looking at **about 8–12 weeks** (roughly 2–3 months). If you want to preserve the tower’s historic appearance, you’ll also need to coordinate with heritage authorities, obtain permits, and schedule work around tourist traffic, which could add extra lead time.
